gap_notes: CORE cannot be scored for aspect *meaning*. Geometry of 0/60/90/120/180 is now compared (Ptolemy I.16/I.27 + Lilly CA I.1). Qualitative labels are not the same system: Ptolemy harmonious/discordant-by-sex vs Lilly good/enmity/concord. Do not collapse.
Lilly CA I.19 opened (printed ~p.105): orbs are planetary moieties, two tables, used from memory. Not aspect-orbs and not an IL object field. Schema not expanded. requires_action still unevidenced.

Lilly: sextile indifferent good; square enmity and not good; trine unity/concord/friendship; opposition a bad aspect; conjunction good or ill according to the question. None of these attest requires_action.

requires_action is boolean in schema (no unknown/not_evidenced). false here means the opened locus does not establish the property — not the assertion 'this aspect does not require action'. Schema not expanded.

Lilly I.19 sharpens I.1: square = imperfect enmity; opposition = perfect hatred; sextile/trine = love/unity (trine stronger); conjunction good/bad as the planets are friends or enemies. Still not Ptolemy sex-harmony. Do not copy into interaction.

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter XXVII (Ashmand p.38–39)
claims.original_claim: When distances are trifling, the preceding planet applies to the following; the same rule holds for bodily conjunction, for which latitudes must also agree.
claims.normalized_claim: Conjunction is bodily application of two bodies in the same parts of the zodiac

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter I Aspects (1659 p.25–26)
claims.original_claim: When two planets are in one and the same degree and minute of any sign, they are in Conjunction.
claims.normalized_claim: Conjunction is 0 degrees: same degree and minute

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter I Aspects (1659 p.25–26)
claims.original_claim: Conjunction is good or ill according to the nature of the question demanded.

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIX Terms and Aspects (1659 p.105)
claims.original_claim: The strongest configurations are sextile, square, trine, opposition; conjunction is called an aspect very improperly.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly I.19: conjunction is not properly an aspect

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIX Terms and Aspects (1659 p.105)
claims.original_claim: Conjunctions are good or bad as the planets in conjunction are friends or enemies to one another.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly I.19: conjunction quality follows whether the bodies are friends or enemies

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIX Terms and Aspects (1659 p.105–107)
claims.original_claim: A partile aspect is exact in degree; a platick aspect is within the moiety of both planets' orbs.
